ending.why: Fresh. Everything the send-back named is gone and nothing aired has come in to replace it: the music does not stop, the lights do not change, nobody is spoken to or singled out, the host does not sing, and the hook's words are the same every time. The aired ending's order of moves (lights down, a spoken stop on the host, a flat line that puts him in, the full band back on a changed hook) has no counterpart here. What the ending is now, in its own moves: a lift of a whole step on the band's 'wop'; a third verse whose subject is the smallest thing on the list; a real three-word post landing as the fifth tile; a copy of its words going up as a banner; the hook unchanged with one more 'doo-wop'; one wide shot with everything in it; then the host's dry line and the two-syllable tag. Checked against the record and clear: the aired song had no key change, no banner and no final frame gathering its pictures, and its button was the host crediting the band and a band member topping him with a reference and a board. Here the host takes the applause for a song he was not in, which is his character and a new joke. A hook that returns with no word changed also takes this song out of the count toward a signature. Three things I looked at harder, none a block. (1) The last verse says a few posted words became something everyone is now inside. That is the nearest thing here to the aired episode's premise (a post, and then the thing exists, with the host and the audience inside it) and to its monologue joke about themed weeks. By mechanism it is neither. The post declares and does not wish; members take a name up and nothing is built; there is no bot, no stock line, no stamp and no time from the post to the week; and the themed week returns as a subject with a different turn (there, two weeks in one day; here, where a week's name came from). It stays fresh only while the banner is a copy of the card's words going up and not a delivery: no stamp, no arrival sound beyond the one ooh, no tag saying how soon. (2) A real member's short post on a card at the piece's warmest moment, with a soft crowd sound, shares a primitive with the aired closing beat (real posts held on cards as the sincere answer to the night's question). The job differs: there the cards answered a question the show had asked all night; here the card is the fifth item of a list, a three-word glance lit on the sung words. Not the same device. (3) In the present running order the song is straight before the chess segment, whose second line is 'It began as one post.' Each is fine alone. Back to back they say one thing twice, and that thing is what the earlier final review asked the next reviewer to listen for being said out loud. That is a matter of order, not of this script, and it is under inside.

message: Yes, and it is more plainly the week's than before: the feeling is now carried only by things the week did (a simulator under a shrug, a mug taken into it, three words taken up as the week's name, and then the band's two syllables as the next thing down), so nothing in it could be sung another week, though with the host gone it has lost the one line where the message was both felt and laughed at and now lands as a warm picture and not as a moment.
inside: One echo helps and one needs distance: the banner's three words are the name the coffee segment's 'polyhedron week comes in many forms' has already used, which works as a callback in either order, but the new small account's handle is very nearly the handle of the small account whose card the coffee segment shows large, so straight after that segment the two heroes can be taken for one person. The echo that matters most is with the chess segment, which in the present order follows at once and opens on 'It began as one post.': the song's last verse has just sung that a few posted words became the whole week, so the same thought is stated twice in a row, and the song therefore wants a place that is neither straight after the coffee segment nor straight before the chess.
airWhy: The alternative: its ending is now clear of what has aired, and although the change cost it its best laugh and leaves it level with the present song on funny, it is still ahead on the other three rows and is the one of the two that says something about the week, provided it is moved out of the slot between the coffee segment and the chess.
